summary: Three controller-owned GitHub admin-watchdog dispatches at head 6c44e5b live-exercised the M11.4 admin_ops_events Cloudflare D1 write paths while read authority rested at supabase. Run 36377157726 (write=d1-canary, canary marker=true) inserted one marked event into D1 only with a 200 on the parameterized insert, and Cloudflare Observability recorded GET /v1/ops/admin-events/latest 200, POST /v1/ops/admin-events 200 and POST /v1/ops/admin-events/prune 200 on Worker version cc448d9b-566c-465a-8ee9-dcfc2aef42c7. Run 36377256343 (same d1-canary + marker) produced the identical watchdog violation signature but Observability shows GET /latest 200 and POST /prune 200 with NO POST /admin-events, proving the read-before-write signature dedupe skipped the second insert while prune still ran on D1. Run 36377461933 (write=d1, canary marker empty) recorded GET /latest 200, POST /admin-events 200 and POST /prune 200 on Worker version 87f3acb5-6843-4118-bb7f-cc0f51a0f5e9, proving the ordinary full-D1 write path (dedupe read + successful insert + prune). Because a selected D1 insert returns 200 only when the parameterized insert actually succeeded (the boundary fails closed otherwise, 503/throws), the 200 responses prove the D1 inserts executed. These bounded write runs do NOT prove a combined full-D1 read/write cutover and do NOT complete M11. The current production reconciliation of Supabase and D1 admin_ops_events at 412/412 with matching latest-20 identity is the post-live clean state: the temporary canary/full-write D1 rows were subsequently deleted/reconciled, and that clean state is NOT evidence that the historical inserts did not happen.

liveRuns.label: bounded-d1-canary-insert
liveRuns.interpretation: the bounded d1-canary selector accepted the explicitly marked event, the parameterized D1 insert returned 200 (the boundary fails closed otherwise, so a 200 means the D1 insert succeeded), the dedupe read resolved to D1, and the prune ran on D1; no ordinary event was routed to D1 and Supabase read authority was untouched

liveRuns.label: d1-dedupe-read-before-write
liveRuns.interpretation: the read-before-write dedupe resolved the same latest signature on D1 and skipped the insert (no POST /admin-events), while prune still ran on D1 (POST /prune 200); this proves the M11.4 dedupe-skipped-insert-while-still-pruning contract against D1

liveRuns.label: ordinary-full-d1-write
liveRuns.interpretation: under full d1 write authority an ordinary (unmarked) event ran the dedupe read on D1, the parameterized D1 insert returned 200 (success), and prune ran on D1; this is the full admin_ops_events D1 write path for an ordinary run
